rows.evidence: Q1: Section 4/4.1 and Figures 6-8 - the authors describe their own prototype (Node.js server, five virtual blockchain nodes, NodeMCU/Arduino sensor nodes), show real-time sensor readings from two fields (Fig. 7) and report their own measured average response time of the system (Fig. 8).
rows.notes: The study designs and prototypes an IoT-blockchain water management system and evaluates only a technical indicator (average response time) plus displays of sensed soil humidity, temperature and water volume used. It never measures trust, coordination, water sharing or cohesion among farmers or communities; those benefits are asserted in the related-work and conclusion sections (e.g., blockchain 'enables' farmers competing for scarce resources to trust the technology) without any survey, observation or test. The sensors are soil humidity, temperature and water-level sensors rather than flow meters per se, though Fig. 7d displays litres used. Q1 is given with some doubt because the Data Availability Statement says no new data were created or analysed.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section 4.1 and Figures 7-8 - own prototype implementation with Arduino-based sensor nodes and a private blockchain of five virtual nodes; authors report their own real-time monitoring plots and the measured average response time for ~45 irrigation indices.
rows.notes: No result on water conservation or water-use efficiency is reported. The study only displays monitored soil-irrigation level (Fig. 7c, 'properly irrigated' at 100%) and litres of water used/remaining (Fig. 7d) and evaluates system response time; there is no comparison of water applied or saved against a baseline, no efficiency metric, and no crop outcome. Claims that the system maximises efficiency are assertions. Monitoring of water volume is at most a precondition for conservation. Sensors are soil moisture/water level rather than flow meters, but water-volume accounting is displayed, so technology mismatch not flagged.

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper is largely conceptual (architecture, design patterns, authentication protocol) with a small prototype demonstration; the Data Availability Statement states that no new data were created or analysed, which casts doubt on treating it as a primary study, but Section 4.1 does report the authors' own prototype runs and response-time measurements. No dispersion measures, limitations, support conditions, multi-site evaluation or scale beyond the prototype fields are reported for either claimed effect.
